title: Spring didn't come for free
takeaway: Every beautiful thing that blooms was watered by someone's sacrifice.
scene: The garden is blooming, and people think it just happened. The poet knows the truth: he fed those flowers with his own blood.

original: اپنا خون جگر دا دتا پھلاں نوں کئی وار
ایویں تے نئیں ایس چمن وچ یارو آئی بہار
transliteration: Apna khoon jigar da ditta phullaan nu kayi vaar
Aiven te nahin is chaman vich yaaro aayi bahaar
translation: Many times I gave the flowers my own heart's blood.
Friends, spring didn't just come to this garden for nothing.
couplets.story: This garden looks beautiful now, but it didn't happen by itself. Again and again, he fed the flowers with his own blood. Spring came because of his sacrifice.

original: گل کیتا اے پیار دا دیوا سجناں پھوکاں مار
سدھراں دے ہن بوہے ڈھو کے چپ دا جندرا مار
transliteration: Gul keeta ae pyaar da deeva sajnaan phookaan maar
Sadhraan de hun boohe dho ke chup da jandra maar
translation: The beloved blew out the lamp of love.
Now I've shut the doors of my longing and locked them with silence.
couplets.story: The Beloved blew out the little lamp of love. So now he has closed the doors of his heart and put a padlock of silence on them.

original: دل دے باغ نوں ساڑ گئے نیں اوہدے نے ہاسے
لوکی کہندے اوہسے تے کھڑ پیندی گلزار
transliteration: Dil de baagh nu saar gaye nain ohde ne haase
Loki kehnde oh hasse te khir paindi gulzaar
translation: The beloved's laughter burned the garden of my heart,
though people say when they laugh, whole flowerbeds bloom.
couplets.story: Everyone says the Beloved's laugh makes flowers bloom. For him, that same laughter burned his heart's garden to the ground.

original: تن میرے دے لوں لوں اندر یاد تیری دیاں مہکاں
اس متوالے دل دے اندر تیرا او سے پیار
transliteration: Tan mere de loon loon andar yaad teri diyaan mehkaan
Is matvaale dil de andar tera oho pyaar
translation: Every pore of my body holds the fragrance of your memory;
in this intoxicated heart, your love is the same as ever.
couplets.story: Every part of his body is filled with the 'smell' of remembering the Beloved. His heart is still drunk on that same love. Nothing has changed.

original: مدہوشی دے پلے پا گئی اک نشیلی اکھ
نہ رنداں دا دامن بچیا زاہد دی دستار
transliteration: Madhoshi de palle pa gayi ik nasheeli akh
Na rindaan da daaman bachiya, zaahid di dastaar
translation: One intoxicating eye threw everyone into a daze:
neither the free spirits' robes were spared, nor the holy man's turban.
couplets.story: One look from those amazing eyes left everyone dizzy. The carefree crowd lost control, and so did the strict religious man. His turban fell off.

original: میرا دل تے سڑ دا بلدا سڑ سواہ ہو جاندا
تیری ذات پیاری سجناں آ پھسی وچکار
transliteration: Mera dil te sarda balda sar suaah ho jaanda
Teri zaat pyaari sajnaan aa phasi vichkaar
translation: My heart would have burned and burned until it turned to ash,
but your dear self, my love, got caught in the middle.
couplets.story: His heart would have burned down to ashes, but the Beloved lives inside it. So it can't burn away completely. The Beloved is caught in the middle.

original: پیار دی نگری پیر نہ پائیے کھس جاندے نے ہاسے
ایویں تے نئیں لوکی کہندے دو دھاری تلوار
transliteration: Pyaar di nagri pair na paaiye, khus jaande ne haase
Aiven te nahin loki kehnde do-dhaari talwaar
translation: Don't set foot in the city of love; your smiles get stolen.
People don't call it a double-edged sword for nothing.
couplets.story: He gives a warning. Don't walk into the city of love. It steals your happiness. There's a reason people call love a sword that cuts both ways.

original: بیڑی نوں پئے سناں لاندے بیڑی دے اسوار
ناخدا دی نیت ماڑی کنج ہوواں گے پار
transliteration: Beri nu pae sannaan laande beri de asvaar
Naakhuda di neeyat maari, kinj hovaange paar
translation: The passengers themselves are drilling holes in the boat,
and the captain means harm. How will we ever get across?
couplets.story: He paints a scary picture. The people on the boat are making holes in it, and the captain wants to sink it. How is anyone going to reach the other side?

original: دیوانے دی چپ نے ڈکیا ہویا شور حشر دا
بول پیا تے چیک پین گے سارے در و دیوار
transliteration: Deewaane di chup ne dakkiya hoya shor hashr da
Bol piya te cheek pain ge saare dar o deewaar
translation: The lover's silence is holding back the uproar of Judgment Day.
If he speaks, every door and wall will scream.
couplets.story: His silence is holding back something enormous. If he ever spoke up about what he's been through, it would be so loud that even the walls and doors would cry out.

original: عاشق لوک انا دے بندے کھوہ دریا نئیں کہندے
ڈبن لگے ڈب جاندے نیں دو ہنجواں وچکار
transliteration: Aashiq lok ana de bande, khooh dariya nahin kehnde
Dubban lagge dubb jaande nain do hanjhuaan vichkaar
translation: Lovers are proud people; they don't make a fuss about wells and rivers.
When they drown, they drown between two tears.
couplets.story: Lovers don't need a huge river to drown in. They're proud and quiet. They can drown in the space between two tears.

original: تڑپ بے چینی ہوکے ہاڑے سدا لئی جگراتے
ہر تے سدھراں دی گٹھڑی دا چکی پھرنا بھار
transliteration: Tarap bechaini hauke haare sada layi jagraate
Hor te sadhraan di gathri da chukki phirna bhaar
translation: Restlessness, unease, sobs and pleas, and sleepless nights forever,
and on top of that, carrying around the heavy bundle of my longings.
couplets.story: His life is full of restless days, crying and endless sleepless nights. On top of all that, he carries his hopes and wishes around like a heavy sack on his back.

original: میں چھلاں نال کھیہ کے احمدؔ کول تیرے آ جاواں
اگلے پاسے کھڑا ایں سجناں واج تے مینوں مار
transliteration: Main chhallaan naal kheh ke Ahmad kol tere aa jaavaan
Agle paase khara ain sajnaan, vaaj te mainu maar
translation: Ahmad, I'll fight my way through the waves and come to you.
You're standing on the far bank, my love; just call out to me.
couplets.story: He ends with a promise. Like Sohni crossing the river, he'll fight through the waves to reach the Beloved. All they have to do is stand on the other side and call his name.

deeper:
The ending is the soul's answer to God: 'Just call me, and I'll cross any river to reach You.' The Qur'an says, 'Call on Me, and I will answer you' (40:60), and Sufis add that the call goes both ways. The seeker only needs to hear God's voice to find the strength to fight the waves.

The boat with holes and a captain who means harm can be read as a warning about false guides. It also warns about a community that damages its own faith from the inside. The lover's silence holding back 'the uproar of Judgment Day' is the restraint of someone who carries deep spiritual pain without complaining.
why: It starts with a striking idea, that every beautiful thing was paid for by someone, and ends with one of the most hopeful images in the book.
prompt: Who has 'watered the garden' in your life without people noticing what it cost them?
notes: A shorter variant of this ghazal is printed on page 55; it is kept here as a variant, not a separate poem.

variant.summary: A shorter version of this ghazal is printed again on page 55. It drops several couplets and opens with a different first couplet, given here.

original: عشق گلاواں گل وچ پا کے ناں کر حال پکار
سدھراں دے سب بوہے ڈھو کے چپ دے جندرے مار
transliteration: Ishq galaavaan gal vich paa ke naa kar haal pukaar
Sadhraan de sab boohe dho ke chup de jandre maar
translation: With love's noose around your neck, don't cry out about your state.
Shut every door of longing and lock it with silence.
extraCouplets.story: Once love has its rope around your neck, don't complain about it out loud. Close the doors on all your wishes and lock them with silence.
